Class StandardPaths

java.lang.Object
io.github.sanyarnd.standardpaths.StandardPaths
public final class StandardPaths extends Object

Collection of methods, which return paths to the most common system locations.

Paths in the documentation are examples: the implementation asks the system (environment, registry, XDG configuration) and returns the real path. Returned paths are absolute, but the directories are not guaranteed to exist. A method returns an empty value if the system has no such directory (e.g. runtime() on Windows) or the path can't be determined (e.g. $HOME is not set).

Use forApp(String) to get directories of the particular application:

AppPaths app = StandardPaths.forApp("my-app");
Path config = app.config().orElseThrow();

    • home

      public static Optional<Path> home()

      Current user home directory:

      • Windows: user.home (%USERPROFILE%);
      • macOS, Linux: $HOME (default: user.home).
      Returns:
      path to the home directory, empty if it can't be determined

    • temp

      public static Optional<Path> temp()

      Directory for the temporary files:

      • Windows: java.io.tmpdir (GetTempPath, usually %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp);
      • macOS, Linux: $TMPDIR (default: java.io.tmpdir, then /tmp).
      Returns:
      path to the temp directory, empty if it can't be determined

    • cache

      public static Optional<Path> cache()

      Directory for the non-essential (cached) data:

      • Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA% (%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local);
      • macOS: $HOME/Library/Caches;
      • Linux: $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default: $HOME/.cache).
      Returns:
      path to the cache directory, empty if it can't be determined

    • config

      public static Optional<Path> config()

      • Windows: %APPDATA% (%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming);

      • Linux: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default: $HOME/.config).
      Returns:
      path to the config directory, empty if it can't be determined

    • data

      public static Optional<Path> data()

      Directory for the application data:

      • Windows: %APPDATA% (%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming);
      • macOS: $HOME/Library/Application Support;
      • Linux: $XDG_DATA_HOME (default: $HOME/.local/share).

      Note that Windows synchronizes the roaming directory with the domain server. If it's not desired, consider using dataLocal() instead.

      Returns:
      path to the data directory, empty if it can't be determined
